Mauritius Electric Utilities Hit by Major Cyber Attack; Service Disruptions Persist

A sophisticated cyber attack targeting key electric utilities firms in Mauritius has triggered widespread service disruptions, with Azure Power Global Ltd among those affected. The incident, which began late Tuesday evening, has left thousands of customers facing intermittent power outages and delayed billing services, as companies scramble to restore their IT infrastructure.

Industry sources indicate that the attack bears hallmarks of a ransomware campaign, with attackers reportedly encrypting critical files and demanding payment for their release. While utility operators have not disclosed the ransom amount, the disruption has hampered daily operations, with customer call centers overwhelmed by inquiries.

Azure Power Global Ltd confirmed in a statement this morning that several of its information systems had been compromised. “Our technical teams are working around the clock to contain the threat and restore normal operations,” the company said. “We apologise to our customers for the inconvenience and assure them that supply restoration is our highest priority.”

National Grid Mauritius, another leading utility, also reported partial outages across the Curepipe and Quatre Bornes regions. “We are experiencing technical difficulties due to a cyber incident and are coordinating with authorities as well as cybersecurity experts,” said CEO Vikash Ramdanee. “We urge our customers to conserve electricity where possible while we address the issue.”

The Mauritius Electrical Workers Union expressed concern about employee safety and job security amid the crisis. “These attacks put immense pressure on our staff, especially those working overtime to manually manage grid operations,” union president Marie Celestine commented.

According to estimates from the Mauritius Utilities Trade Association, as many as 40,000 households and businesses have been impacted by interruptions or delayed services since the onset of the attack. Analysts note that while the island’s power sector has made significant investments in digital transformation, the rapid integration of IT systems has also increased exposure to cyber threats.

“Electricity supply is critical to both the economy and public welfare,” said Kiran Mungur, an independent energy analyst. “This incident highlights the urgent need for enhanced cybersecurity across the industry.”

As of press time, authorities and affected companies continue to work on restoring full functionality, with no official timeline for complete recovery. The Cybercrime Unit of the Mauritius Police Force has launched an investigation into the source and scope of the attack.
